newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares extend gains, seen up on Friday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares extend gains, seen up on Friday.

text.p: Polish shares rose on Thursday for the second straight session and analysts said the dominant buying after price-fixing signalled prices were attractive enough for the bourse to extend gains on Friday.

The main market's all-share WIG index rose 0.6 percent to 14,423.8 and turnover fell 20.7 percent to 68.1 million zlotys ($23.5 million) on both markets. Gainers led losers by 45 to 21 with 17 stocks flat.
Analysts said the market, which has risen 8.5 percent since December 10, might be benefiting from the expectation that investment funds would buy more at the start of the year.

"That's a possibility, but we'll have to see how turnovers go, because they're low now, possibly because some investors might have taken a vacation during the short week," said Ryszard Wojnowski, an analyst at Bank Gdanski brokerage.
Analysts said investors may have already priced in the central bank's comments it might raise interest rates as early as mid-January to curb fast credit growth.
They said top gainer carpet maker Novita surged 9.5 percent after it sold a stake in a subsidiary.
They said construction firm Espebepe surged 9.3 percent in speculative demand, as the firm still had financial problems.
Analysts also said meat-processing firm Sokolow, up 7.5 percent in active trade, may have been helped by its Thursday statement it sought a strategic investor.
Mass privatisation NFI units rose 0.7 percent to 143.5 zlotys ($49.5) but fell the same amount to 145 zlotys ($50) in 9.1-million-zloty ($3.2 million) continuous trade.
